item.description: "There's a lot of people who are really interested in the nation's history and bobbleheads are a perfect way for that," Phil Sklar said.

item.description: "I think we really have to think politically and really think about our values and what we need to protect there," Michael Livermore said.

item.title: Federal CIO outlines ‘one government’ blueprint for overhauling digital services
item.description: Federal Chief Information Officer Greg Barbaccia said his top priority is to get the federal government to “obsess over delivering tangible outcomes."

item.title: Virginia senators call for investigation into DHS use of personal data
item.description: The senators pointed to reports that DHS and ICE are tapping into tools ranging from facial recognition and license plate readers to social media monitoring.

item.title: GSA ends U.S. participation in ‘open government’ initiative
item.description: GSA argued the initiative was ineffective. Civil society experts say it’s another example of the Trump admin turning its back on openness and transparency.

item.title: Resilience is essential as demands on government networks multiply
item.description: Agencies can’t predict the next attack, new mandates or the next cloud outage. But they can control the strength of their network foundation.

item.title: MSPB: Tenured employees can’t be fired under probationary period rules
item.description: An administrative judge says CISA violated the rights of a tenured employee when they fired him using the rules for probationary employees.

item.title: Agencies prepare for partial shutdown, as lawmakers look to minimize its impact
item.description: The Senate passed a spending package on Friday, based on a compromise reached between President Donald Trump and congressional Democrats.

item.title: Senate passes Trump-backed government funding deal, sending to House
item.description: The Senate has voted to fund most of the government through the end of September while carving out a temporary extension for Homeland Security funding, giving Congress two weeks to debate new restrictions on federal immigration raids across the country. With a weekend shutdown looming, President Donald Trump struck the spending deal with Senate Democrats on Thursday in the wake of the deaths of two protesters at the hands of federal agents in Minneapolis.
